# Contributing to PhoneDrop

Thanks for helping. PhoneDrop is small on purpose: one tray exe, no iPhone app, nothing running when nothing is happening. Contributions that keep it that way are very welcome.

## Where to start

| You want to | Do this |
|---|---|
| Pick a small task | Take a [good first issue](https://github.com/mynameishaheer/phonedrop/labels/good%20first%20issue) (a few hours each). Comment on it so nobody doubles up. |
| Do something bigger | Open an issue or a [Discussion](https://github.com/mynameishaheer/phonedrop/discussions) before writing code. Planned work: [ROADMAP.md](../docs/ROADMAP.md). |
| Report a security bug | **Not in an issue.** Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and report it privately. |

By taking part you agree to the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Build and test

You need Go 1.24 or newer on any OS. Most of the code doesn't need Windows.

```sh
scripts/build.sh              # go test ./..., then cross-compiles phonedrop.exe
go test -race ./...           # what CI runs
GOOS=windows go vet .         # vets the Windows-only files from Linux or macOS
gofmt -l .                    # must print nothing
```

The code is in `cmd/phonedrop/`. Files ending `_windows.go` only build for Windows. Everything else is portable and tested on Linux in CI, so keep logic that doesn't need Win32 there.
Code map: [DEV.md](../docs/DEV.md). Wire protocol, the contract between PC and shortcuts: [PROTOCOL.md](../docs/PROTOCOL.md).

## The rules

1. **Standard library only, no cgo.** No third-party Go modules; Windows APIs go through `syscall`. This keeps the exe small and the supply chain empty. (The one external tool, `go-winres`, is run by hand to regenerate the icon and version resource; see `scripts/build.sh`.)
2. **Idle must cost nothing.** No polling loops, no tickers while the panel is hidden, no background timers. Block on accepts and channels; check expiry lazily.
3. **Stream, don't buffer.** Received files go to disk as they arrive.
4. **Never log secrets, signatures, file names or text contents.** Users paste the log into issues.
5. **Protocol changes need a spec change.** Update `docs/PROTOCOL.md` (and the shortcuts guide and generator, if the phone side changes) in the same pull request.
6. Match the surrounding style: `gofmt`, short comments that say *why*, compact code.

## Previewing the UI

`phonedrop.exe -preview <folder>` renders every panel state (ready, paused, pairing, recent list, outbox and so on) to PNG files without opening any window.
It works on real Windows and under Wine, which is enough for layout and spacing; colours and fonts only look right on real Windows.
Attach before and after PNGs to pull requests that touch the UI.

## The iPhone shortcuts

The shortcuts are written by hand in [SHORTCUTS.md](../docs/SHORTCUTS.md), and the same six are generated by [shortcuts/build.py](../shortcuts/build.py) (Python 3, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I shortcuts/build.py          # writes shortcuts/unsigned/*.shortcut and validates them
python3 -I shortcuts/build.py --check  # validates only
```

- The generator checks that every file parses, every If/Repeat is closed and every variable is set before use.
- Output is deterministic, so a rebuild without changes gives identical files.
- Apple only imports **signed** shortcuts, and signing needs a Mac (`shortcuts/sign-all.sh`). If you change the generator, say in the pull request whether you could sign and run the result on an iPhone.
- Keep the guide and the generator in step: they describe the same shortcuts.

## Commits and pull requests

- One logical change per commit. Subject line in the imperative, about 70 characters, with an optional area prefix, as in the existing history: `Shortcuts: store If comparison values as text tokens`. Explain *why* in the body when it isn't obvious.
- Add or update tests for behaviour changes. Tests for the portable code run on every push.
- Before opening a pull request: `gofmt -l .` is empty, `GOOS=windows go vet .` and `go test -race ./...` pass, and docs are updated. The pull request template has the checklist.
- Windows-only changes: say which Windows version you tried them on.
- New user-visible behaviour gets a line under `[Unreleased]` in [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md).
